hero.headline: Glydways proposes elevated self-driving transit connecting West Palm Beach to airport
hero.teaser: A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. Glydways will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration.
hero.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The elevated system would connect President Donald J. Trump International Airport to the convention center and nearby Brightline and Tri-Rail stations using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads. The system would bypass traffic congestion, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes, with estimated travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity, referencing previous South Florida light rail estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. The company described it as functioning like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without intermediate stops. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting will determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing, with a planning and design contract potentially awarded later this year.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion state budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of shrinking spending plans in Florida. The budget includes nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, with DeSantis stating he is not trying to set a record after vetoing a record-breaking $3.1 billion in 2022. The Governor said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. DeSantis touted these priorities while also setting aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades. The cuts included $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers salaries. The Legislature had also proposed transferring $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement, but that transfer was among the items cut.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to veto 621 projects worth $830 million that the group labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations the group wanted eliminated. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, prompting the Legislature to include the potential $750 million transfer this year.

DeSantis, who is term-limited, also indicated he does not plan to be formally involved with any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals. He said if someone asked him to do something, he would not refuse, but he will not lead the effort himself. The budget takes effect as DeSantis prepares to leave office after serving as Florida's Governor.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
cards.teaser: A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, and South Florida drivers are feeling it. AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with heavy rain complicating an already crowded holiday on South Florida roads. AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Friday's wet weather made for a tough start to the holiday weekend on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando, with driver Ed Budd noting that rain causes drivers to forget how to drive.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. Experiences varied on the road: Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday and reported smooth sailing with no traffic or accidents. Meanwhile, driver Fernando Amado described a very different experience, saying it's been pretty busy, especially with the weather. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents demand fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as dispute heads to budget talks
cards.teaser: A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach access point is creating tension between Colony Condos residents and beachgoers. The town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons, and residents say people are now cutting through their private property.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer with cars parking in private spots and people cutting through bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs.

Hill said residents used to confront trespassers but now call police because people get rude. The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, suggesting a combination of split rail and shrubs.

The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15. Hill said residents are hoping the town will put the fence back up so they can have their landscaping and private parking restored.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is opposing a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following controversial Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, constituted a "serious offense" that justified his removal.

Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling establishing that disciplining teachers for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violates First Amendment protections. She recommended Theobald be reinstated and awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald acknowledged writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority over Theobald's employment status, with no timeline announced for a decision. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises a larger question about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Let Late Lead Slip Away in 10-3 Loss to Tarpons
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover P
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park.

Tampa scored six unearned runs in the eighth inning, capitalizing on four Mets errors, then added three more runs in the ninth to pull away on Independence Day. The Tarpons extended their winning streak to eight games, while St. Lucie dropped its ninth straight.

The Mets led 3-1 entering the eighth after building the advantage with timely offense and strong relief work. But Tampa's comeback began after Hans Montero reached and eventually scored the tying run when Bryce Martin-Grudzielanek hit a two-out ground ball to third baseman Branny De Oleo. The ball deflected off De Oleo's glove for an error, allowing Montero to come home and even the game at 3-3.

The inning continued from there, and David McCann delivered the decisive blow with a three-run home run off Conner Ware to give Tampa a 6-3 lead. McCann struck again in the ninth, launching another three-run homer off Luis Alvarez to make it 10-3.

McCann finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk and seven RBI. The performance came one day after he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.

St. Lucie had trailed 1-0 early before tying the game in the fourth inning on an RBI groundout by Simon Juan. Chase Meggers gave the Mets a 2-1 lead in the fifth with a two-out RBI single against Tyler Boudreau. Juan then added a solo home run off Boudreau in the sixth to stretch the lead to 3-1.

Ware had kept Tampa quiet through three scoreless innings before the eighth-inning unraveling. He took the loss after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings, though all five were unearned.

Tampa reliever Jose M. Rodriguez earned the win after pitching a perfect seventh inning.

The Mets fell to 2-10 in the second half and 35-43 overall. Tampa improved to 11-3 in the second half and 46-34 overall.

The teams close their six-game series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m. It will be Little League Day. Little leaguers who wear their jerseys will receive free admission and a gift courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. Riviera Beach was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The National Civic League announced the award during its conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying residents are seeing "the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do."

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment. These include the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of the community. City leaders said the designation positions the community for future opportunities and sends a message to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration drives results.

cards.headline: S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach jumps from C to A rating as Palm Beach County schools earn third straight A
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County earned an A rating from the state for the third year in a row. S.D. Spady Elementary School made a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year.
cards.body:
For the third consecutive year, the School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education. This year, 143 district-operated schools, representing 84% of the district, received "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate, with 86% of seniors participating in college-level coursework, including Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary in Delray Beach led the district's success stories, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served as principal for 15 years after five years as assistant principal, attributed the turnaround to curriculum modifications made three years ago. The school restructured its early childhood program, which begins at age 3 and combines with kindergarten, with those students now in third grade and performing at higher levels. Spady was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year, alongside Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% as ground beef and strawberries see biggest increases
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition is getting more expensive this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year. Inflation is driving most of the price increases. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, buns are up 7.7%, and ice cream is up 5.3%. Strawberries have been hit particularly hard, up 12.4% due to a Florida frost.

Not all cookout staples have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, benefiting those planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies to manage costs. She suggests comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for items on your shopping list and emphasizes that cutting down food waste is crucial for families, starting with a meal plan.

hero.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
hero.body:
The Martin County School Board is resisting a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher who was suspended over social media comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, faced discipline after posting remarks on Facebook that characterized Kirk as racist, misogynistic, and a neo-Nazi.

In court filings submitted Thursday, the school board's legal team argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone made errors in recommending Theobald's reinstatement. The board contended that numerous conclusions in the judge's decision lack adequate factual support. The school board's attorney maintains that the Facebook post about Kirk constituted a serious violation that justified removing the teacher from his position. The board emphasized that the offense warranted the disciplinary action taken against Theobald.

The judge's recommendation relied on a recent ruling from the Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal establishing that disciplining teachers for personal Facebook posts created away from school, using personal devices, and without student involvement violates First Amendment protections. In her order from last month, Livingstone recommended not only that Theobald be rehired but also that he receive back pay and benefits for the period of his suspension.

According to an investigation report reviewed by WPTV, Theobald acknowledged writing the comments about Kirk but explained the posts appeared on his mother's private Facebook page as part of a conversation among people he knew personally. He stated the comments were not intended to reach a wider public audience. Following the judge's recommendation, Theobald raised broader concerns about where schools should establish boundaries regarding teachers' speech outside the workplace. The school board retains ultimate authority to decide whether to reinstate Theobald, and no timeline has been announced for when the board will make its final determination. The case highlights ongoing tensions between protecting educators' personal freedoms and maintaining school district standards for employee conduct.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road with 7-acre land transfer
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike. The city is working on multiple phases of the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase and construction is anticipated to begin in Summer 2027.

FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange for the Turnpike. The partial interchange is still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce offers tours, art classes and artist residencies
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce is transforming the city into an artistic destination. The non-profit organization preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain in the historic Crain Estate and connects local and international artists.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation, located in the historic Crain Estate, preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain. Mr. Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The estate remains largely unchanged from the Crains' time there, with many original features intact including the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and stained glass. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items including a gazebo shipped from India. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven of them. The property now has over 100 peacocks. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and known for walking with a limp. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations. Art director Krystal Masters leads one-on-one classes in the art lab for children and adults of all skill levels, featuring mediums including sculpting and watercolor.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of only 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson credited the award to a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents and belongs to all of them. Officials said being named an All-America City sends a message to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration drives results.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit and their decision to wear life jackets. Deputies responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged. Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation to nearly double capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be completed by next Fourth of July. The year-long undertaking will nearly double the dock's capacity, increasing the number of slips from 18 to 44 for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The improvements will consist of a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded through a state grant and transportation impact fees. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades serve a purpose beyond adding capacity. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it." During the closure, Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will be able to continue running. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city allowed the company to build a gate at the non-floating section of the dock to board passengers. Kuyrkendall emphasized the dock's importance, stating "Stuart is not Stuart without the water." Boat captain Parker Fisher, who is based in Stuart, supports the project, saying it has needed work and suggesting the addition of more floating docks.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday after injuring her right knee during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old lost her singles match 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday. In an Instagram post, Serena said she was heartbroken to withdraw from doubles, stating that the opportunity to play alongside Venus meant the world to her. "I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete," she wrote.

Serena posted images of four syringes showing the fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in a first-round doubles match that had been pushed back to give Serena more recovery time. Despite the withdrawal, Serena hinted at future competition, saying "stay tuned to a city near you" with the U.S. Open approaching. Venus, 46, played in mixed doubles on Friday with Kevin Krawietz but lost in straight sets. The Williams sisters are six-time women's doubles champions at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time, advances to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and defending World Cup champion Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in South Florida, advancing to face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday.
cards.body:
Argentina's go-ahead score came in the 111th minute when Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges for an own goal. Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run from Lisandro Martinez's lofted pass and hammering a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha. Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde, both equalizers that stunned the pro-Argentina crowd. Vozinha, the 40-year-old goalkeeper, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Cape Verde became the smallest country to reach the knockout round after securing draws against Spain, Uruguay, and Saudi Arabia.

Messi now has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race as the top scorer. He has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak. Argentina will face Egypt, which beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday, in Atlanta on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state championship after 10-2 season and district title
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for the 2026 fall season with their sights set on a state championship. After finishing last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, a second-round playoff exit has motivated the program to pursue deeper postseason success. Head coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of his senior class, noting that most are four-year seniors who came through the middle school program. "They know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

The Scots are taking a deliberate approach to improvement by scheduling more challenging opponents this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained that the demanding schedule is designed to elevate the program's competitiveness. "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete," Williams said. The team's focus has shifted from regular season success to advancing further in the playoffs. Senior Jack Whelche emphasized this priority, stating that going undefeated in the season matters less than avoiding another second-round playoff exit. Senior Edmyer St. Jean credited the summer workout program as crucial preparation, saying the daily grind builds momentum toward breaking the program's record.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Let Late Lead Slip Away in 10-3 Loss to Tarpons
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover P
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park.

Tampa scored six unearned runs in the eighth inning, capitalizing on four Mets errors, then added three more runs in the ninth to pull away on Independence Day. The Tarpons extended their winning streak to eight games, while St. Lucie dropped its ninth straight.

The Mets led 3-1 entering the eighth after building the advantage with timely offense and strong relief work. But Tampa's comeback began after Hans Montero reached and eventually scored the tying run when Bryce Martin-Grudzielanek hit a two-out ground ball to third baseman Branny De Oleo. The ball deflected off De Oleo's glove for an error, allowing Montero to come home and even the game at 3-3.

The inning continued from there, and David McCann delivered the decisive blow with a three-run home run off Conner Ware to give Tampa a 6-3 lead. McCann struck again in the ninth, launching another three-run homer off Luis Alvarez to make it 10-3.

McCann finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk and seven RBI. The performance came one day after he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.

St. Lucie had trailed 1-0 early before tying the game in the fourth inning on an RBI groundout by Simon Juan. Chase Meggers gave the Mets a 2-1 lead in the fifth with a two-out RBI single against Tyler Boudreau. Juan then added a solo home run off Boudreau in the sixth to stretch the lead to 3-1.

Ware had kept Tampa quiet through three scoreless innings before the eighth-inning unraveling. He took the loss after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings, though all five were unearned.

Tampa reliever Jose M. Rodriguez earned the win after pitching a perfect seventh inning.

The Mets fell to 2-10 in the second half and 35-43 overall. Tampa improved to 11-3 in the second half and 46-34 overall.

The teams close their six-game series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m. It will be Little League Day. Little leaguers who wear their jerseys will receive free admission and a gift courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Programs Through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach Country Club Hosts Fourth of July Fireworks and Pool Party
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors celebrated Independence Day with family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event included a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers said this years event also recognized Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities began with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests could enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families could take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games.

Live music from Solstice Reign was expected to begin around 6 p.m. Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course would offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse also hosted a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida State Parks waive admission fees through Sunday for America's 250th anniversary
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection waived admission fees at state parks from Friday, July 3, through Sunday, July 5, to celebrate America's 250th birthday.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is waiving admission fees at Florida State Parks from Friday, July 3, 2026, through Sunday, July 5, 2026, to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. All residents and visitors can explore the parks for free during this weekend, with opportunities for hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding. The parks also feature historic sites including forts, battlefields, archaeological sites and other historic landmarks.

Three parks are excluded from the free admission promotion: Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park. Free admission applies to day use only, and all other fees remain in effect, including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals. The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the National Recreation and Park Association's National Gold Medal Award. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks saw more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated 3.6 billion dollars in statewide economic impact. For park locations and details, visit FloridaStateParks.org or America250FL.com.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion state budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of shrinking spending plans in Florida. The budget includes nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, with DeSantis stating he is not trying to set a record after vetoing a record-breaking $3.1 billion in 2022. The Governor said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. DeSantis touted these priorities while also setting aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades. The cuts included $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers salaries. The Legislature had also proposed transferring $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement, but that transfer was among the items cut.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to veto 621 projects worth $830 million that the group labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 out of the 621 appropriations the group wanted eliminated. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, prompting the Legislature to include the potential $750 million transfer this year.

DeSantis, who is term-limited, also indicated he does not plan to be formally involved with any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals. He said if someone asked him to do something, he would not refuse, but he will not lead the effort himself. The budget takes effect as DeSantis prepares to leave office after serving as Florida's Governor.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities celebrate America's 250th with fireworks and parades
cards.teaser: Fourth of July weekend brought fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations across Southwest Florida as communities marked America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Fourth of July weekend is bringing fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations across Southwest Florida as communities mark America's 250th birthday. Festivities span from Sarasota's bayfront and Nathan Benderson Park to Manatee County, Venice, North Port and Fort Myers Beach. The Privateers, a local nonprofit focused on support for youth programs, will host its annual parade and water fight tradition in the Coquina Beach and Bradenton Beach area. Bradenton and Palmetto are celebrating together with activities along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest at Riverside Park will feature 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a kids zone and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the Manatee River.

Sarasota will host its America250 fireworks display at the bayfront beginning at 9 p.m. Waterside Place in Lakewood Ranch will celebrate with circus acts, carnival games, a kids zone, food and a drone show over the water at 1560 Lakefront Drive at 9 p.m. Siesta Beach will host its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m. with fireworks launching at dusk, funded 100 percent by local residents, businesses and community supporters. Venice will celebrate America250 and the city's centennial with a patriotic parade through Historic Downtown Venice beginning at 9:30 a.m. at West Venice Avenue and Avenue des Parques. Fort Myers Beach will kick off celebrations with a parade starting at 10 a.m. at Bay Oaks Recreation Center, heading down Estero Boulevard to Times Square, with fireworks launching from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m.

cards.headline: North Port celebrates Independence Day at CoolToday Park with Freedom Festival
cards.teaser: CoolToday Park hosted North Port's Independence Day celebration with patriotic entertainment, family activities, food vendors, live music and fireworks.
cards.body:
The Freedom Festival: Cheers to 250 Years event ran from 6 to 9:30 p.m. on Villages Parkway, with fireworks scheduled for 9 p.m. conditions permitting. The celebration included patriotic entertainment and family activities as North Port marked America's 250th anniversary.

Downtown Fort Myers celebrated the semiquincentennial with a free concert by Deb The Dynamics and a fireworks and drone show at the Caloosa Sound Amphitheater. The event ran from 7 to 9:30 p.m. at 2101 Edwards Drive. Punta Gorda hosted Fourth Fest celebration at Laishley Park with live music, family activities, food and beverages and fireworks at 120 Laishley Court, with fireworks starting at 9 p.m. The event page noted there would be no continuous running waterslides this year due to ongoing water restrictions.

Longboat Key hosted the Longboat Key Freedom Fest featuring the Shortest Parade in America, a rededication of Bicentennial Park and the Hot Diggity Dog costume contest at Bicentennial Park, 2730 Gulf of Mexico Drive. The St. Regis Longboat Key Resort hosted an elevated evening oceanfront BBQ dinner and fireworks display at 1601 Gulf of Mexico Drive.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce preserves historic Crain Estate and hosts global artists
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is establishing Fort Pierce as an artistic destination by maintaining the historic Crain Estate and supporting the Peacock Arts District. The nonprofit preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who originally owned the property. Jaxson Crain worked as a tile worker, and his skilled craftsmanship remains visible throughout the facility in the flooring, walls, and ceilings. Guided tours of the gardens and distinctive architecture are available on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. The foundation has deliberately kept the estate largely unchanged from the Crains' era, maintaining approximately 90 percent of the property in its original condition. This commitment reflects a conscious decision to preserve the estate's authentic character without pursuing commercialization. The smoking and bourbon room exemplifies this preservation approach, featuring distinctive man paneling, masculine color schemes, and stained glass windows that open onto a front patio bar.

The Crains were world travelers who journeyed globally nine times, acquiring unique items for their Florida home. Among their international purchases was a gazebo shipped from India, which features decorative peacocks in its design. The foundation is currently restoring the gazebo's base to match its original painted pattern. The estate's name derives from the peacocks inhabiting the property for decades. The Crains introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce during the 1970s, beginning with seven birds that have since multiplied to over 100. One particularly notable peacock named Bob, believed to be 60 years old, is recognizable by his distinctive limp. Bob resides at the facility in his own designated space with personal bowls and receives hand-feeding from tour guides daily. Staff members note that peacock interactions create memorable experiences, particularly for young visitors who feed the birds from their hands. The estate also has historical connections to monkeys, as one story recounts that Jaxson Crain brought a baby monkey back from South America in his pocket.

The artist-in-residency program draws creative professionals from around the world to work at the foundation. Participating artists receive simple yet elegant accommodations on the property that provide everything necessary for their stay. The foundation's art lab offers classes for both children and adults regardless of experience level. Art director Krystal Masters conducts one-on-one instruction designed for complete beginners, allowing students to develop skills in various mediums including sculpting and watercolor. Classes range from specialized workshops such as "Paint Your Pet in Watercolor and Rainbow" to personalized projects matched to individual interests.

Masters emphasizes that art serves therapeutic purposes beyond creative expression. She describes art as a stress-relieving activity that leaves participants feeling fulfilled and engaged. Students complete classes with finished artwork that generates genuine satisfaction and connection. This philosophy guides the foundation's educational mission, ensuring that visitors to the Peacock House leave having experienced both artistic growth and personal renewal.
